explanation: In C++, operator overloading allows developers to define custom behaviors for operators when applied to user-defined types such as classes or structs. Overloading the inequality operator (operator!=) enables intuitive comparison of objects by specifying how to determine if two instances are not equal. This enhances code readability and aligns object comparison semantics with built-in types, especially in object-oriented programming where object state comparisons are common.
syntax: ReturnType operator!=(const ClassType& rhs) const noexcept;
